text:
Large language models (LLMs) are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They learn patterns in language by predicting the next word in a sentence, much like a very advanced autocomplete system. When you type a prompt, the model uses these patterns to generate a logical response.

Prompt engineering is the skill of writing clear, specific instructions to get the best results from an LLM. For example, asking “Summarize this article in three bullet points” is better than just saying “Help me.”

These models can write essays, answer questions, and translate languages, but they have limits. They don’t truly understand meaning and can make confident mistakes. Also, their knowledge stops at a certain date, so they aren’t always current.
